entries.english:
In the year of the Lord 1224, indiction twelve, on Monday, the seventh day of October, at Bolzano, in the episcopal palace, in the presence of Lord Gotsahic, provost of Augsburg, Lord Vivianus, Conrad of Greifenstein, Frederick of Rosenpach, and others. There Lord Count Albert of Tyrol, acting as assessor of Lord Bishop Gerard, set a hearing date for Lord Bertoldus Suapus, present as guardian of the children of the late Massarius, so that within fourteen days, on the following day, he would answer and render an account to Litoldus, son of Videpach, in a tithe case before the gastaldus appointed by the lord bishop at Bolzano.

I, Tridentinus, notary of the Sacred Palace, by leave and authority of the venerable father Lord Henry, by the grace of God and of the Apostolic See bishop of Trento, faithfully and lawfully drew this aforesaid instrument from the abbreviated notes of the late Peregrinus, notary of Bolzano, the original note of this instrument having been cancelled, and reduced it to public form, adding or removing nothing that would change its meaning or sense; I placed my sign and subscribed.

facts.subject: Friedrich de Rosenpacho
facts.content: is listed in the charter concerning the tithe dispute.

entries.summary: In Bolzano, a proceeding under the authority of Count Albert of Tyrol involves a summons before the bishop’s judicial official in a tithe dispute. Federicus de Rosenpacho is listed in the charter.
